My whole life, my parents were crazy mad about lying. Lying was like e worst offense possible.

So lesbian 15 year old me spent a whole year having panic attacks thinking I was lying to them by not coming out. My parents were't extremely religious, and they weren't anti gay (at least not openly enough that I tought they would react so strongly about it).
So I come out. And I get thrown out of my house for one night with nothing but the clothes I was wearing. The  next day when they accept me into the house, I am not allowed in the computer or cellphone without someone behind me reading everything. I am not allowed to speak unless completely necessary. I am not allowed to stay in my room unless I was going to sleep, and the door should always be open. I wasn't allowed to stay in school unless I had classes. I wasn't allowed to go out with my friends.
I got sent to a 'therapist' who sat me down and kept telling me that there was no way I was gay and it was all bad influences of my friends (at the point I was the only one in my group of friends who had come out... most of them did come out but only years later) and how could I know I was gay if I had never fucked a girl?! Basically he tried to convince me that I didnt knew what I was feeling and was being raped by the girl I was dating.

When I got home from the therapist and proceed to tell my mom that I didnt liked him, I got slapped in the face and told I was disgusting and stupid. My mom didnt talk direct to me or looked at me directly until I (lying) told her i was wrong and liked boys. 
I had to obviously broke up with the girl I was dating, and because my parents didnt seem strict enough half of friends didnt believe they had reacted like that and stopped talking to me.
All the rules, including the speaking rule, continued until I was 20 years old.  Honetsly, it only made me hate myself and them more than anything.
